question.problem: Consider a triangle $△ABC$, where an exterior angle at $A$ is ${100}^{∘}$ and an exterior angle at $B$ is ${122}^{∘}.$ What is the measure of the interior angle $C?$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw a corresponding picture.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191822/assets/b1d04d90855560e36762d492f34ac14fb960c98f55c234da7c706e638fd9ea9e.png)

   

Let $z$ be the measure of the exterior angle at $C$ pictured above. Since the sum of the exterior angles of a triangle is ${360}^{∘}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{100}^{∘}+{122}^{∘}+z & ={360}^{∘} \\ {222}^{∘}+z & ={360}^{∘} \\ z & ={138}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can find the value of the missing interior angle at $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠C & ={180}^{∘}-z \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{138}^{∘} \\  & ={42}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $m∠C={42}^{∘}.$
